instructions: Assess only the listed primary candidates in a fresh invocation. Read their dialogue first, then the exact card; use the alternate only to judge meaningful differentiation. Supply six criterion ratings with specific turn evidence and full coach-2.0 findings. Do not invent missing backstory or assume earlier approval. No writer scores or rationales are supplied. Report real reservations and failures. Totals are calculated in code.
productionStandard:
PRODUCTION STANDARD coach-2.0. Historical coach-1.0 acceptance is not coach-2.0 acceptance. Read the dialogue first and record what the spoken words establish before interpreting the card. Exact cards are already in this invocation: label internal-dialogue-first, never blind or human review. Do not invent a charitable backstory; harmless unspecified names/history are not defects. Fill coach2 for ORIGINAL dialogue in writer output and CANDIDATE dialogue in reviewer output. Copy the supplied dialogue hash for the text being assessed. Give concise actual turn evidence, not generic claims.
G1: legible immediate situation, wants/stakes; separate stated, ordinary inferred, and missing essentials. Identify first material defect or explicitly none.
G2: coherent facts, ownership, timing, language, knowledge; recognizable misunderstanding/revelation is allowed, unstated intervening events are not.
G3: assess all A1-B2, B2-A3, A3-B4, B4-A5 links. Vocabulary repetition alone is insufficient. Purposeful avoidance must read as behavior.
G4: B is a plausible participant with an intelligible practical/emotional position, not a contrived punchline cue. B can help, concede or solve.
G5: exact card changes A's choices. For pairs Stance changes HOW A pursues Drive and B responds to the merged behavior; neither card may be decorative.
G6: ending develops the same behavior using B4. Investigate if A5 would work after unrelated B4; more obstacles are not required for heightening.
format: five spoken ABABA turns, existing word/schema limit, no narration/coaching/truncation.
Every mandatory gate and transition is PASS, FAIL or UNCLEAR with evidence; UNCLEAR cannot be accepted. All gates pass AND total >=85 AND fidelity/response >=4 AND others >=3; preserve the six weights 30/20/15/15/10/10. A 5 is not merely presence. Totals are derived in code. Retain good originals; no rewrite quota. Review both alternatives for different tactics, relationships or pressure. Scene outline identifies roles, task, A want, B want, stakes, exact-card tactic and B's contribution; it is private planning evidence, not a substitute for missing spoken facts. Humour must come from sincere priorities and responsive choices, not stock hierarchy or unrelated slogans. Record actual weaknesses and reservations. Writer corrections target only rejected/materially changed scenes; preserve all accepted records and prior original assessments exactly. No coach-1.0 failure or exhausted allowance is erased by this separately versioned cycle.

card.title: What Does the Winner Get?
card.instruction: Accept competitive claims, but keep asking who benefits, who pays, and what actually changes after the result.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So winning best garden means I open it to visitors on Sunday?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. Our club keeps the admission money.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And who pays me for opening the gate and cleaning up?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody. But as winner, you join the committee that decides how we spend it.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does that committee meet here too? I need to know whether I've won a vote or another room to clean.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely trophy. Who pays to insure it while it's in my house?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The winner. We can display it here if you'd rather.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Does that transfer the insurance bill to the club?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Yes. We'd ask you to polish it before open days.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: How many open days? I'd like to compare the insurance with the unpaid shifts.

card.title: One Point Changes Everything
card.instruction: Choose one tiny advantage, score, concession, or technicality and treat it as the decisive fact in every choice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: We're not leaving the quiz until my missing half-point is restored.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We lost by thirty. I've booked dinner.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Move the booking. That half-point decides whether this evening was worth coming out for.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The scorer can email a correction tomorrow.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then book dinner tomorrow. I won't choose our celebration restaurant without the final half-point.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My cake has one extra cherry. Put it in the winner's photograph.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The flavour winner wasn't burnt. Yours was.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Photograph my extra cherry close up. That's the deciding advantage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Then readers will want your recipe. Can I leave out the decorations?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leave out anything except that cherry. I won't have readers following my winning recipe and ending up tied.

card.title: The Contest Beneath Everything
card.instruction: Interpret each new event as another move in a much larger competition whose true winner may not be visible yet.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You bought lunch again. You're building quite a lead in this friendship.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You helped me move. I'm thanking you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've made my entire moving day worth one lunch. Excellent bargaining.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Come to ours for Christmas. Nobody's keeping score.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You're bringing the whole family into it. I'll bring breakfast for Boxing Day; this won't be decided over one turkey.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: The neighbour returned my ladder cleaned. That's a move in the gardening rivalry.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Perhaps it was just dirty.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Now my ladder is cleaner than my windows.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You could say thanks.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Concede the first round? Not before I've polished his wheelbarrow.

card.title: Command with an Escape Hatch
card.instruction: Carry yourself as though every decision settles the matter, while preserving one ambiguity that lets you later reverse what the decision meant.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your garden party is approved for a small gathering. Go ahead.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wonderful. I've invited fifty people.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Small means everyone fits round our table. The approval stands.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I'll borrow a bigger table.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Our table means the one we own. Tell the others their invitations are for another small gathering.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You may borrow the car for a short trip. That's settled.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Wonderful. I'll drive forty miles to the airport.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Short means the station at the end of our road. You're approved for that.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That works. I'll park there until I fly back next week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Short includes the car's stay. Return it before you catch the train. The permission stands.

card.title: Authority Changes Hands
card.instruction: Project control while guarding one detail that could transfer authority elsewhere. Let each return of that detail shift whom you defer to or overrule.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll chair the club meeting unless that signed result names someone else.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It names me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course. May I ask you to check the date, Chair?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're right. My term starts next month.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I'll take questions. Yours first, if you raise your hand.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Rehearsal starts at six. Unless someone else has a room key, that's final.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The caretaker gave me one. I want to start at five.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Five it is, then. May I check which door yours opens?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The outer door. You'll still need to unlock the rehearsal room.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then six it is. You may assemble everyone outside at five; I'll admit you when we're ready.

card.title: The Expert Blind Spot
card.instruction: Perform mastery everywhere except one specific subject. Deflect it at first, reinterpret it later, and let each return increase the pressure.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've explained the engine's fuel feed and cooling. Leave that red switch; we'll cover it later.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I need to start it for the demonstration.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: First, let me show you the beautifully simple throttle linkage.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: The audience is here. The label says START.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's the manufacturer's interpretation. Before we endorse it publicly, I'll explain why the engine is currently stopped.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've explained the deposit and repairs in your lease. Renewal can wait.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Renewal is why I brought it. Do I need to do anything?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Let's establish your excellent grasp of the deposit first.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: It says 'renews automatically.' I'm calling the landlord now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Put me on speaker. 'Automatically' describes a process, and I'll need him to define his terms.

card.title: Insider with the Wrong Memories
card.instruction: Act like an unquestioned insider while offering details that almost fit. Treat each contradiction as proof the group, system, or relationship changed.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I'll put our gardening trophy in the old cupboard beside the piano.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We keep prizes on that shelf. We've never had a piano.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Open shelving. You've modernised since I organised the rose show.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I founded this club last month. Tonight's our first meeting.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A fresh founding date too. Shall I give the new members some history before we put it all behind us?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: At our old reunions, Uncle Frank always carved the turkey.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Nobody here has an Uncle Frank.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Families edit their history so quickly now.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You're at the wrong reunion.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: That's a remarkably efficient way to describe how much you've changed.

card.title: I Meant to Teach That
card.instruction: Treat any correction, surprise, or improvement as evidence your teaching succeeded. Claim each reversal as the lesson you intended all along.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Excellent. You spotted the deliberate error in my recipe.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You baked it that way yesterday.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: A demonstration is more memorable than a warning.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: You ate three slices.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Commitment to the lesson. I'm glad you're questioning authority now.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You've improved my filing system. Just the independence I hoped to provoke.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Your system lost every invoice.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: And yours has found them. The learning journey is complete.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I did it by ignoring you.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: My most advanced outcome. I'll include it in the course description.

card.title: The Favor Not Yet Named
card.instruction: Behave as though you hold decisive leverage, but delay naming it until another explanation has taken root.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before you explain why I shouldn't join the committee, shall I keep this envelope closed?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What's in it?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Tell me your reasons first. They sound carefully prepared.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: We only admit people who contribute to the building.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then perhaps now is the moment for my receipt for its new roof.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Go on explaining why you can't help me move. I'll save my little reminder.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: What reminder?

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your reasons should have a fair chance without interference.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Moving is something people should arrange themselves.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Lovely principle. Shall we apply it to the piano I moved for you?

card.title: Same Memory, Different Meaning
card.instruction: Return to one shared memory as comfort, then evidence, then accusation, changing its meaning without abandoning the facts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Remember when you saved me the window seat? I thought I mattered to you.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I knew you liked the view.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Exactly. Proof that you noticed small things.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Also, I needed the aisle seat to stretch my bad knee.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So my fondest memory of being understood was your knees negotiating space.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Before my exhibition, I keep thinking how you hung my first painting. It makes me feel safe here.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Still in the hall. I point it out to everyone.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: So that's proof you believed in me before the reviews.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I tell them even you had to start somewhere.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You hung it to reassure everyone else they couldn't possibly do worse.

card.title: The Debt Changes Hands
card.instruction: Treat every favor as shifting who owes whom. Recalculate the balance whenever help is accepted, refused, or remembered.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: You fixed my bike, so I owe you dinner.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I was repaying the dinner you cooked last week.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then your repair was too good. I owe you for the surplus kindness.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Please don't cook again.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Now you're saving me work. The debt has increased.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Your parcel's upstairs. We're even for yesterday's lift.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: That's yours. I brought it in from the rain.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Then I owe you twice. I'll take your rubbish down.

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Three flights with a leaking bag? That clears both debts.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Leaking? That puts you in debt. You can repay me by cleaning the stairs behind me.
